deep.reconstruction:
Caveat on authorship. This folio is not Riemann's own mathematics. It is a later commentator's account of Riemann's treatment, in a letter, of the Pfaff problem as Gauss formulated it. The commentator writes in the first person ('wie ich und andere vor mir', 'Ich stelle es so (p. 523)', 'zeige ich dann p. 525/7'). The page numbers 239/240 match Gauss's 1815 review of Pfaff's 'Methodus generalis' in Gauss, Werke III. The commentator's 523–527 refer to a publication of their own, which I have not identified.

Setting (from the previous page). The Pfaffian form is Ω = Σ_{σ=0}^{n-1} p^σ dx^σ, with x^0 = x and p^0 = p. The bilinear covariant is [ρ,σ] = ∂p^ρ/∂x^σ − ∂p^σ/∂x^ρ, which is skew.

Gauss's reduction keeps x as the distinguished variable. It leads to equations 3) and 5), written as:
[ρ,0] + Σ_{σ≥1} [ρ,σ] ∂x^σ/∂x = M p^ρ, for ρ = 0..n-1.
This is a linear system of n equations in the n unknowns ∂x^σ/∂x (σ=1..n-1) and M.

Top of page. The previous page noted that the skew determinant |[ρ,σ]| vanishes identically for odd n, and may also vanish for even n; in that case the system forces M = 0. The page adds a second condition: the bordered determinant with columns [ρ,1]..[ρ,n-1], p^ρ must not vanish. Otherwise equations 3), 5) do not deliver actual values of the ∂x^σ/∂x. Riemann's version of the condition is that x = const must not follow from them.

The commentator's conclusion: Gauss's transformation problem, even for even n, can neither always be reduced to the equations 6) R/p = R'/p' = … nor always be solved. The image reads 'weder … noch'; see the corrections.

Generalized problem (the commentator's own, 'p. 523'). Seek independent functions x^σ(α, y^0, …, y^{n-2}) such that Ω = (1/N) Σ_{i=0}^{n-2} q^i dy^i, with every q^i independent of α.

Derivation (the intermediate steps are filled in by me):
1. Substitute to get Ω = A dα + Σ_i B_i dy^i, where A = Σ_σ p^σ x^σ_α and B_i = Σ_σ p^σ ∂x^σ/∂y^i.
2. The requirement is A = 0 together with ∂(N B_i)/∂α = 0 for i = 0..n-2.
3. By the chain rule and the skewness of [ρ,σ]:
∂B_i/∂α − ∂A/∂y^i = Σ_ρ (∂x^ρ/∂y^i) · Σ_σ [ρ,σ] x^σ_α.
4. Define v_ρ = Σ_σ [ρ,σ] x^σ_α + p^ρ ∂log N/∂α. Given A = 0, the conditions ∂(N B_i)/∂α = 0 read v · ∂x/∂y^i = 0 for each i.
5. Also v · ∂x/∂α = Σ [ρ,σ] x^ρ_α x^σ_α + A ∂log N/∂α = 0. The first term vanishes by skewness, the second because A = 0.
6. The Jacobian ∂(x)/∂(α,y) is nonsingular, so v = 0.

This gives the system on the page:
α) Σ_σ p^σ ∂x^σ/∂α = 0,
β) Σ_σ [ρ,σ] ∂x^σ/∂α + p^ρ ∂log N/∂α = 0, for ρ = 0..n-1.
These conditions are necessary and sufficient.

Converse. Contracting β) with ∂x^ρ/∂α gives 0 + A · ∂log N/∂α = 0. Hence α) follows from β) exactly when β) does not force ∂N/∂α = 0. The page states precisely this.

Finally the commentator states, as shown in their own pp. 525–7, that α) and β) can always be satisfied by independent functions when n is even. So the generalized problem is always solvable for even n.

The next page explains why Riemann sets N = e^{-s} and writes the system in differential form, k^ρ = Σ[ρσ]dx^σ − p^ρ ds = 0 and ω = 0. That form handles the case ∂log N/∂α = 0.
errors: No mathematical error. The equivalence of α), β) with the transformation requirement checks out, given the nonsingular Jacobian. The converse statement (α follows from β iff ∂N/∂α ≠ 0) is exactly right: contraction with ∂x/∂α yields A·∂logN/∂α = 0.

The sentence beginning 'von denen, …' is partly struck out and syntactically incomplete. It apparently intended to say that one of the n+1 equations is redundant, namely that α) follows from the others.

results.what: Criticism of Gauss's reduction of the Pfaff problem to the equations R/p = R'/p' = … The reduction fails when the skew determinant vanishes (always for odd n, possibly for even n) or the bordered determinant vanishes, because then M = 0 or x = const is forced.
results.modern_name: Pfaff problem; rank/class of a Pfaffian form (bilinear covariant, skew matrix [ρ,σ])
results.usually_credited_to: Pfaff 1815, Gauss's review 1815, Jacobi 1827; rank/class theory by Frobenius 1877 and Darboux 1882

results.what: Necessary and sufficient conditions α), β) for Ω = N^{-1} Σ q^i(y) dy^i with q^i independent of α, and the solvability of this system for even n.
results.modern_name: First reduction step of the Pfaff problem: a characteristic (Cauchy) direction lying in the kernel of ω ∧ dω-type conditions; reduction of a Pfaffian form in n variables to n−1 variables up to a factor
results.usually_credited_to: Pfaff/Jacobi; systematic treatment by Clebsch (1861–63), Natani (1859), Frobenius (1877)

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics is standard 19th-century Pfaff-problem theory, and the page is a third-person commentary by a later author, not Riemann's own work. Its interest is historical: it documents that Riemann, in a letter, analysed Gauss's reduction and its failure cases (insisting on ds ≠ 0 and on keeping ω = 0). That is a modestly notable but not major detail.

checkable.sympy: from sympy import *; a,y=symbols('a y'); u,v=symbols('u v'); P0=Function('P0'); P1=Function('P1'); X0=Function('X0')(a,y); X1=Function('X1')(a,y); p0=lambda X,Y: P0(X,Y); p1=lambda X,Y: P1(X,Y); A=p0(X0,X1)*diff(X0,a)+p1(X0,X1)*diff(X1,a); B=p0(X0,X1)*diff(X0,y)+p1(X0,X1)*diff(X1,y); br=(diff(P0(u,v),v)-diff(P1(u,v),u)).subs({u:X0,v:X1}); rhs=diff(X0,y)*(br*diff(X1,a))+diff(X1,y)*(-br*diff(X0,a)); simplify(diff(B,a)-diff(A,y)-rhs)
checkable.asserts: For n=2: ∂B/∂α − ∂A/∂y = Σ_ρ ∂x^ρ/∂y Σ_σ [ρ,σ] ∂x^σ/∂α, with [0,1] = ∂p0/∂x1 − ∂p1/∂x0. The expression should simplify to 0.

checkable.sympy: from sympy import *; M=Matrix(3,3,lambda i,j: Symbol('m%d%d'%(min(i,j),max(i,j)))*(1 if i<j else (-1 if i>j else 0))); simplify(M.det())
checkable.asserts: A skew-symmetric determinant of odd order vanishes identically (here order 3), as cited on the previous page.

checkable.sympy: from sympy import *; n=4; S=Matrix(n,n,lambda i,j: Symbol('s%d%d'%(min(i,j),max(i,j)))*(1 if i<j else (-1 if i>j else 0))); xa=Matrix(symbols('xa0:4')); simplify((xa.T*S*xa)[0])
checkable.asserts: Contracting β) with ∂x/∂α kills the [ρ,σ] term by skewness, leaving only A·∂logN/∂α. This is why α) follows from β) unless ∂N/∂α = 0.

transcription_corrections: Lines 9–11: the image reads 'Das Gauß'sche Transformationsproblem läßt sich also bei geradem n weder stets auf die Gleichungen 6) zurückführen, noch auch überhaupt stets lösen'. The transcription has 'stets … und auch überhaupt stets lösen', which reverses the meaning.

Lines 1–2: 'diese[?] wirkliche[?] Werthe' should probably read 'nur wirkliche Werthe' or 'bestimmte wirkliche Werthe'. The derivative is most likely ∂x^σ/∂x, the variable of the previous page; the transcription has ∂x^σ/∂α.
Lines 2–3: the reading is '(oder (Riemann) wenn aus ihnen nicht x = const. folgen soll)', with 'wenn' inserted above the line.
In the struck passage after β): the transcription's 'wenn α) eine eine Folge' contains a duplicated 'eine'. The surviving text reads '…, wenn α) eine Folge der übrigen ist'.
